Let me analyze this OIML certificate for water meters.

Certificate details:
- Number: R49/2006-SK1-14.03, Revision 1
- Member State: Slovakia
- Issuing Authority: Slovak Legal Metrology, Hviezdoslavova 31, 974 01 Banská Bystrica, Slovakia
- Person responsible: Jaromír Markovič (title: Ing. Jaromír Markovič, PhD.)
- Date issued: 5 November 2014
- Scheme: This is an OIML-CS certificate... Actually R49/2006-SK1-14.03 is a basic OIML certificate (not the newer CS scheme with A/B). The schema has scheme (A|B). This certificate predates the CS scheme. Hmm. The scheme field says "scheme (A|B)". For older certificates, we might omit it or... Actually the recommendation section has "scheme" too. For older certs, the scheme is not A or B — the OIML-CS scheme A/B applies to CS certificates issued after 2017. This one is from 2014. I could omit scheme or set it to null. Rules say "If a field is not present in the markdown, omit it." So omit scheme.

- Project number: not present. The test report numbers are 2013/MI-001/B076/001 and 2014/MI-001/B047/312.03 (and also mentioned 2014/MI-001/B047/001 in section 7 — slight discrepancy; page 1 says "2014/MI-001/B047/312.03 having 58 pages" and section 7 says "Test report No 2014/MI-001/B047/001"). I'll extract both test reports as given.

Test reports:
- 2013/MI-001/B076/001, 64 pages, role: type_evaluation_report (or test_report)
- 2014/MI-001/B047/312.03, 58 pages, role: test_report
- Also 2014/MI-001/B047/001 in documentation section

Applicant: Ningbo Aimei Meter Manufacture Co., Ltd., 68, West Town Road, Shangtian Town, Fenghua City, Zhejiang, 315511 P.R. of China
Manufacturer: The applicant (i.e., same). So manufacturers[]: name "Ningbo Aimei Meter Manufacture Co., Ltd." with same address, or "The applicant". I'll list the same name/address.

Certified type:
- Category: Water meter (the schema example list includes "Gas meter", so "Water meter" fits). Actually the category list: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter", ... — I'll use "Water meter".
- type_designations: ["ML-A", "ML-AP"]
- module_designation: null (not applicable — this is a complete water meter)
- description: "Mechanical multi-jet dry dial water meter intended for metering the volumes (consumption) of clean cold water in residential (households) and commercial use. It is installed into pipe lines in horizontal installation positions."

Model family: The cert covers ML-A and ML-AP types across DN 15, 20, 25, 32, 40, 50 with various R ratios. The models vary by DN and ratio.

Table structure:
DN 15: Q3 = 2.5 m³/h; Q1 values: 0.03125, 0.025, 0.02, 0.015625 corresponding to R = 80, 100, 125, 160; Q2 = 1.6×Q1: 0.05, 0.04, 0.032, 0.025; Q4 = 3.125
DN 20: Q3 = 4; Q1: 0.05, 0.04, 0.032, 0.025; Q2: 0.08, 0.064, 0.0512, 0.04; Q4 = 5
DN 25: Q3 = 6.3; Q1: 0.07875, 0.063, 0.0504, 0.039375; Q2: 0.126, 0.1008, 0.0864 (hmm, 0.0864 seems odd — Q2 = 1.6 × Q1, so 1.6 × 0.0504 = 0.08064, but table says 0.0864; and 1.6 × 0.039375 = 0.063). I'll just record as given: 0.126, 0.1008, 0.0864, 0.063. Q4 = 7.875
DN 32: Q3 = 10; Q1: 0.125, 0.1, 0.08, 0.0625; Q2: 0.2, 0.16, 0.128, 0.1; Q4 = 12.5
DN 40: Q3 = 16; Q1: 0.2, 0.16, 0.128, 0.1; Q2: 0.32, 0.256, 0.2048, 0.16; Q4 = 20
DN 50: Q3 = 25; Q1: 0.3125, 0.25, 0.2, 0.15625; Q2: 0.5, 0.4, 0.32, 0.25; Q4 = 31.25

Ratio Q2/Q1 = 1.6 throughout.

So models = combinations of (type ML-A/ML-AP, DN, R ratio). That's 2 types × 6 DN × 4 R = 48 variants. That's a lot. Maybe model_id = "ML-A DN15 R80" etc. Hmm, that's 48 models. That's verbose but complete. Alternatively, treat DN as the model axis: 6 models per type = 12 models, and ratio as a config axis.

Let me think about what's most useful. The schema:

- model_family.models[]: one entry per variant. 48 entries would be exhaustive. Alternatively 12 models (2 types × 6 DN) with R as config_level axis.

Actually, the flow rates vary by R ratio within a DN. So Q1 and Q2 vary across both DN and R. config_level with two axes? The schema says config_level[]: attribute, axis, values[]: {condition, value}. I could do:

- model_level for attributes that vary by model (DN, Q3, Q4, connection thread, construction length) — models identified by type+DN (12 models: ML-A DN15 ... ML-AP DN50). Wait, but the table applies to both ML-A and ML-AP (the Type row says "ML-A / ML-AP" spanning all).

- config_level for Q1 and Q2 which vary by R ratio: axis "ratio_q3_q1", conditions "R80", "R100", "R125", "R160" per model. But config_level values don't reference models... Hmm.

Alternative: 48 models in model_level. Let me consider verbosity. 48 models × Q1 + 48 × Q2 = 96 value entries, plus q3/q4 etc. It's long but accurate. Actually maybe I can be smarter: model_id like "DN15/R80". And the type ML-A vs ML-AP only differs in housing material (brass vs plastic body), so models could be at DN×R level with type as attribute.

I think a reasonable approach:
- model_family.family_name: null (or "ML-A / ML-AP")
- models: 12 entries: model_id "ML-A DN15", ..., "ML-AP DN50"? Or keep at DN level: "DN15"..."DN50" with type noted.

Hmm. Given the type row says "ML-A / ML-AP" spans the whole table, the metrological data applies to both types. The only difference is housing (brass for ML-A, plastic for ML-AP). So models could be DN × R = 24 combos, each available as ML-A or ML-AP.

I'll do 24 models: model_id like "DN15 R80", "DN15 R100", ..., "DN50 R160". That gives precise Q1/Q2 values per model. And model_level entries for nominal_diameter, permanent_flowrate_q3, overload_flowrate_q4, minimum_flowrate_q1, transitional_flowrate_q2.

Let me compute values:

- R160: Q1=0.15625, Q2=0.25

Matrix tables: preserve the full table. I'll create matrix_tables entries:
1. "Metrological data DN15-DN20" — or better, one matrix table for the flow data with columns: nominal_dn, permanent_flowrate_q3, minimum_flowrate_q1, transitional_flowrate_q2, overload_flowrate_q4, ratio_q3_q1, ratio_q2_q1. Rows per model (24 rows).

2. "Dimensions and general characteristics" — columns: nominal_dn, connection_thread, construction_length... rows per DN (6 rows).

Alternatively, one combined matrix table. Let me build:

matrix_tables:
[
  {
    "name": "Flow characteristics by nominal diameter and ratio",
    "columns": ["model", "nominal_diameter", "permanent_flowrate_q3", "minimum_flowrate_q1", "transitional_flowrate_q2", "overload_flowrate_q4", "ratio_q3_q1", "ratio_q2_q1"],
    "rows": [24 rows with model ids and values]
  },
  {
    "name": "Dimensions and general characteristics",
    "columns": ["nominal_diameter", "connection_thread", "construction_length", "installation_orientation", "water_temperature_range", "maximum_working_pressure", "maximum_permissible_error_upper_range", "maximum_permissible_error_lower_range", "scale_interval", "capacity_of_calculator", "mechanical_class", "climatic_class"],
    "rows": [6 rows]
  }
]

Values as structured objects? The schema example in the R137 case used plain numbers in matrix_tables rows ("qmax": 4.0). So matrix table rows can use plain values (numbers/strings). But rule 2 says every characteristic value must be structured... The R137 example shows rows with plain numbers. I'll follow the example: plain values in matrix_tables rows (with column_units carrying units), but structured values in characteristics.model_level and type_level.

Hmm, but the schema for matrix_tables shows "columns[], rows[] (object per row), description, footnotes[]" — the R137 example added column_units. I'll include column_units.

Construction length: "165/190" for DN15 — that's two options (165 or 190 mm). I'll record as string "165/190" or as a list? In matrix rows, string "165/190" is fine. For characteristics... construction length varies by DN — model_level with values as strings? Hmm, rule 2 says numbers not strings, but "165/190" is a list of options. Could be {min:165,max:190}? No — it's alternatives, not a range. I'll keep as string "165/190" in matrix rows only, and maybe skip construction_length in model_level to avoid confusion. Actually including it as string values in model_level seems acceptable (value can be string per rule: "Formulas/symbols. When the value is a formula... keep it as a string"). "165/190" is a list of alternatives; string is reasonable.

Connection thread varies by DN: G ¾ B, G 1B, G1 1/4B, G1 1/2B, G2B, "G2 1/2B / Flange ISO7005". These are strings — model_level with string values? Rule 2 forbids pure unit cells but these are real values. I'll put connection_thread and construction_length in matrix_tables rows and also as model_level string values. Hmm, to keep model_level clean with numeric flow data, maybe just include them in matrix table. Actually the schema's model_level expects {model, value, footnote_markers}; value can be string. I'll include connection_thread and construction_length in model_level too — it's informative. But then it duplicates the matrix table. The rule says matrix_tables preserve multi-dim tables "that don't fit elsewhere". Connection thread fits model_level fine. So maybe only the flow table needs... no wait, the flow table also fits model_level (attribute × model). Hmm.

The R137 example emitted BOTH matrix_tables AND model_level for the same data. So duplication is expected. OK, I'll do both.

type_level characteristics:
- water_temperature_range: {min: 0.1, max: 50}, "°C" (the table says "0,1 to 50" — cold water meter, temperature 0.1 to 50 °C)
- maximum_working_pressure: 16, "bar"
- maximum_permissible_error_upper_flow_rates_range: ±2 at Θ ≤ 30°C, ±3 at Θ > 30°C. This is config-ish. I could do type_level with value "±2" and separate for "±3"? Better: config_level with axis "water_temperature":
  - {attribute: "maximum_permissible_error_upper_flow_rates_range", axis: "water_temperature", values: [{condition: "≤30°C", value: -2... }]}
  
  Hmm, ±2% — structured: value could be {min: -2, max: 2}? MPE ±2% means error between -2% and +2%. I could use value: {min: -2, max: 2}, unit "%". Or keep "±2" as string. The rule about ranges: "±2" is really a symmetric tolerance. I think {min: -2, max: 2} is defensible but might be over-interpretation. Let me use value: 2, unit "%"? Loses the ±. Hmm.

  I'll use config_level:
  ```json
  {
    "attribute": "maximum_permissible_error_upper_flow_rates_range",
    "axis": "water_temperature",
    "values": [
      {"condition": "Θ ≤ 30 °C", "value": {"min": -2, "max": 2}, "unit_symbol": "%"},
      {"condition": "Θ > 30 °C", "value": {"min": -3, "max": 3}, "unit_symbol": "%"}
    ]
  }
  ```
  Hmm wait, the config_level values format: schema says values[]: {condition, value}. Units per value entry — rule 5 says "Values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}". OK.

  Actually for MPE I think string "±2" might be safer... but rule says numbers not strings when numeric. ±2 is a bound pair effectively. I'll go with {min:-2, max:2}. Hmm, but some extractors would keep ±2. The examples in rules: "-10°C/+40°C" → {min:-10, max:40}. By analogy "±2" → {min:-2, max:2}. I'll do that.

- maximum_permissible_error_lower_flow_rates_range: ±5 → {min:-5, max:5}, "%"
- scale_interval: 0.00005, "m³"
- capacity_of_calculator: 99999.99995, "m³"
- mechanical_class: "M1"
- climatic_class: {min:-10, max:55}, "°C" — labeled climatic class with unit °C, value "-10 to +55". attribute name "climatic_class_temperature_range"? The table says Climatic class / °C / -10 to +55. I'll use attribute "climatic_class" with value range and unit °C. Or "temperature_range_climatic_class". I'll keep "climatic_class" value {min:-10,max:55} unit °C. Hmm, that's slightly odd since class usually M1... but the table gives it that way. Maybe better: "climatic_class_temperature_range". I'll use "climatic_class_temperature_range".
- installation_orientation: "H" (horizontal)
- ratio_q2_q1: 1.6, dimensionless
- accuracy class 2 — from recommendation accuracy_classes: [2]. Also could be type_level "accuracy_class": 2. The recommendation has accuracy_classes[] — I'll put [2] there. Maybe also accuracy_class in type_level? Redundant; keep in recommendation.

Ratio Q3/Q1 (R) varies per model: values 80,100,125,160 — that's part of model identity (model_id includes R). I could also add model_level "ratio_q3_q1" per model. That's redundant with model_id but complete. I'll include it in matrix rows and skip as separate model_level to reduce noise. Actually, let me include it — it's in the matrix table anyway. Hmm, I'll include in matrix rows only.

Components: The description mentions essential parts: measuring mechanism, mechanical register, housing, adjustment device, magnetic coupling. Optional: strainer, non-return valve, pulse output with reed sensor switch. Should these be components[]? The schema says "include ONLY if cert names sub-assemblies". These are internal parts described, not certified sub-assembly types. I could add components with roles: measuring_mechanism, register, housing... The description doesn't give type designations for them. I think it's reasonable to include components with role and description-level details. Let me add:

components:

- role: "mechanical_register", type_designations: [], characteristics: {type: "dry type, digital drum with gearing mechanism", digits: 5 (6 for DN40/DN50), pointers: 4}

]
